findings.title: OpenDiscoveryTrace provides useful Git-addressable sample-level scientist-agent evidence packages
findings.observation: At public main 8d42ed3d6a5f0209ef057d80c3e93251da1e941d, OpenDiscoveryTrace publishes Git-addressable JSON samples containing task, ground truth when available, model, structured trajectory records, final claim/confidence, error state and collection metadata. These samples can be inspected in scheduled Chat without rerunning the original model or tools.
findings.scope_guard: This positive claim is sample-level static observability only. The complete 522-trajectory collection is hosted separately and was not established here as a quota-zero transport, and frontier/open-weight trajectory generation itself requires external API/GPU execution.

findings.title: OpenDiscoveryTrace current harness can silently collapse a multi-action model response into one executed/structured step
findings.observation: The public parser scans a whole model response and overwrites parsed PHASE/THOUGHT/ACTION/ACTION_INPUT fields as later declarations appear. The generation loop executes at most the single parsed action, and if any final claim is parsed it records a conclusion and breaks before executing earlier action declarations in the same response. It also stores raw_response only up to 3000 characters. In dd_e01_gpt-5.4 and dd_e01_claude-opus-4.6, structured metadata reports one conclusion step and zero tool calls although raw_response contains several declared api_call/python_exec blocks and OBSERVATION text.
findings.scope_guard: This is an observed parser/execution coherence failure class, not a claim that every published trajectory has the mismatch.

findings.title: Tool-name provenance must distinguish simulated/model-knowledge placeholders from executed external observations
findings.observation: OpenDiscoveryTrace's current execute_web_search explicitly returns a simulated placeholder based on model knowledge rather than real web retrieval. Its python dispatcher passes ACTION_INPUT directly as Python code, while dd_h01_gpt-5.4 supplies a JSON wrapper containing a code field, producing a syntax error. Therefore a handoff cannot infer evidence semantics from a declared tool label alone; executor semantics and exact input/output binding are required.

findings.title: OpenDiscoveryTrace aggregate success provenance is heterogeneous and should not be treated as uniform per-trajectory verification
findings.observation: The published analysis JSON summarizes all 372 frontier trajectories but the success comparison has n=43/42/42 by model rather than n=124 each; medium difficulty has success_rate 0.0 and hard difficulty has success_rate null. The sample files also leave verification.method as pending. The headline approximately-69-percent success therefore should not be promoted to a claim that all 372 trajectories received one uniform completed verifier without first binding the analysis filtering/scoring path.
findings.scope_guard: The exact filtering mechanism has not yet been reconstructed from analysis source in this invocation.

findings.title: Audit-Closed AI Scientist implements a strong public-log-only deterministic admission mechanism
findings.observation: At public main 1e844d1bca18d7bb298aa198e1250bb07bd7ea44, acceptance_from_public_log verifies the hash chain, genesis alpha schedule, exactly one committed candidate set, unique candidates, no uncommitted/duplicate/missing evaluations, transcript thresholds, and then deterministically accepts iff the maximum logged e-value crosses the computed threshold. evaluate_epoch commits a digest of the data before candidate evaluation, and replay_epoch recomputes decision fields from the log. Security tests explicitly reject payload, prev-hash, alpha, commitment and entry-deletion tampering.

findings.title: Audit-Closed paired benchmark is stronger than its currently published static per-trial evidence package
findings.observation: The benchmark implementation uses the same synthetic data and candidate set for baseline batch selection and audit-closed selection in each run and requires replay/integrity success before counting the audit decision. The committed aggregate result also records config SHA-256, seed registry, sample sizes, runtime/dependency versions and a source SHA-256 manifest. However the visible results directory contains aggregate result files rather than the per-trial serialized transparency logs needed for a scheduled-Chat auditor to reconstruct every trial. The documented reproduction path requires Python/package execution.
findings.scope_guard: The mechanism and aggregate provenance are strong positive design evidence, but the currently observed public package is not a complete zero-execution per-trial replay archive.

findings.title: Repository-object-bound decision transcripts are a promising Chat-native replacement for executable replay in simple deterministic admission rules
findings.observation: The audit-closed design shows that an acceptance decision can be a pure function of committed candidate names, logged e-values and an alpha schedule. For Phase-1, a per-trial transcript whose bytes are individually bound by immutable repository blob/tree identity could let scheduled Chat read the exact transcript and recompute candidate_count, alpha_epoch, threshold, ranking and accepted/rejected status without Python. This replaces execution replay with declarative decision replay for this narrow arithmetic decision class.
findings.scope_guard: This is a next-step architecture candidate, not yet an accepted general mechanism. Git-object identity can establish repository-bound content identity but does not by itself provide independent witness nonrepudiation against a repository rewrite.
